name: First Opium War
short_desc: Britain defeats Qing forces and compels China to accept new trading concessions and the cession of Hong Kong Island.
date_note: The first war ended with the Treaty of Nanjing in 1842. It is separate from the Second Opium War of 1856–1860.
notes: Added after a catalog gap review on 24 October 2026. A central turning point in China’s nineteenth-century relations with imperial powers, missing despite substantial Qing and rebellion coverage. Evidence and date rationale: The first war ran from 1839 to 1842 and ended with the Treaty of Nanjing. It is separate from the Second Opium War of 1856–1860; this record does not bridge the intervening peace as one war. Primary evidence: https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/education/teaching-resources/hong-kong-and-the-opium-wars/. Cached Wikipedia introduction and lead image provide separately attributed background. Remains review, not comprehensive factual approval.
